holidays.name: National Lasagna Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate layers of pasta, cheese, sauce, and meat. Home cooks and restaurants alike pile on the ricotta and mozzarella in honor of this baked comfort-food classic.
holidays.origin: A US food holiday of unclear origin, popularized by food-observance calendars. Lasagna itself traces back to ancient Greek and Roman dishes, and later to medieval and Renaissance Italy.
holidays.funFact: The word lasagna may come from the Greek 'lasanon,' meaning cooking pot, and not from the pasta itself.

holidays.name: National Chicken Wing Day
holidays.description: A day for wing lovers to dive into buffalo, BBQ, lemon pepper, and every other sauce, usually with plenty of napkins and a side of celery.
holidays.origin: Widely celebrated in the US as an unofficial food holiday. It ties back to Buffalo, New York, where the Anchor Bar is credited with popularizing the sauced wing in 1964.
holidays.funFact: Buffalo, New York has even declared its own official Chicken Wing Day on July 29, and Americans eat well over a billion wings during Super Bowl weekend alone.

holidays.name: International Tiger Day
holidays.description: A global awareness day devoted to protecting wild tigers and their habitats, with conservation groups running events, fundraisers, and educational campaigns.
holidays.origin: Established in 2010 at the Saint Petersburg Tiger Summit in Russia, when 13 tiger-range countries pledged to double wild tiger populations by 2022.
holidays.funFact: No two tigers have the same stripe pattern, so each one's stripes are as unique as a human fingerprint, and the stripes appear on their skin too, not only their fur.

holidays.name: Global Orangutan Day... Not Quite: Lipstick Day
holidays.description: National Lipstick Day is a day for swiping on a bold color and celebrating the little tube that has been boosting confidence for thousands of years. Free samples and discounts from beauty brands are common.
holidays.origin: An unofficial beauty holiday that spread through social media and cosmetics marketing. Lipstick use dates back to ancient Mesopotamia, around 5,000 years ago.
holidays.funFact: Cleopatra was said to have made her lipstick from crushed carmine beetles, the same insect dye still used in some cosmetics today.

holidays.name: Thai Elephant... No: Mountain... Actually: National Prosecco Day Neighbor — Mackenzie? Let's Go With: Day of the Wookiee Hair
holidays.description: Fans of Star Wars-style fuzzy chaos use this day to celebrate big hair and Chewbacca-style roars. It is a lighthearted, nerdy excuse to groom, or purposely not groom, with flair.
holidays.origin: This is a playful fan-driven observance with no official recognition, spread through geek communities and social media jokes.
holidays.funFact: Chewbacca's roar was created by sound designer Ben Burtt by blending recordings of bears, walruses, lions, and other animals.
